chatbot.q: How is it different from a chatbot?
chatbot.a: A chatbot follows a fixed script. The orchestrator understands the task, chooses a model or agent, calls your systems and performs actions — and logs every step.

localOnly.q: Can we use only local models?
localOnly.a: Yes. The orchestrator works with open-source models deployed on your servers, without external APIs.

cost.a: Routing sends simple tasks to cheaper models, frequent answers are cached, and the console shows the cost of every request and scenario.

duration.a: A pilot on one scenario takes 2–4 weeks. Then we add scenarios and integrations step by step.

mistakes.q: What if the model makes a mistake?
mistakes.a: Guardrails check answers before they are sent, sensitive actions require confirmation, and every decision can be traced and corrected.

cta.title: Let us show the orchestrator on your process
cta.lead: We'll pick one scenario and launch a pilot.

knowledge.q: How does the agent learn about our products and rules?
knowledge.a: We connect your knowledge base, catalogue and policies, and the agent answers from them. Updates are picked up automatically.

unhappy.q: What if a customer is unhappy or asks for a human?
unhappy.a: The agent immediately hands the conversation to an operator with a summary and history, so the customer doesn't have to repeat anything.

oneChannel.q: Can we start with just one channel?
oneChannel.a: Yes — that's how we usually start: with the busiest channel. Others are added later without rework.

brand.q: How does the agent speak in our brand voice?
brand.a: We describe tone, wording and forbidden topics, test them on real conversations and refine them during the pilot.

effect.q: How do you measure the effect?
effect.a: By the share of requests resolved without an operator, response time, CSAT and conversion — compared with the period before launch.
